steps.body: A sorting rule asks a yes-or-no question. The picture asks whether a shape has 4 sides, then sends it to YES or NO.
steps.narration: A sorting rule asks a yes-or-no question. The picture asks whether a shape has 4 sides, then sends it to YES or NO.

widget.prompt: Sort each shape by its number of straight sides.

items.label: triangle
items.feedback: Three straight sides and three corners — a triangle.

items.label: square
items.feedback: Four equal straight sides — a square belongs with the 4-sided shapes.

items.label: rectangle
items.feedback: Four straight sides, two long and two short — still four.

items.label: small triangle
items.feedback: Size is non-defining; three sides still means triangle.

widget.missFeedback: Count the straight sides on each shape before placing it.
widget.successFeedback: Sorted by sides — a defining attribute, so every group really is alike.

predict.prompt: Shapes are sorted by colour instead. Will each group contain only one kind of shape?
predict.reveal: Colour is non-defining, so a red triangle and a red square land in the same pile — only sides and corners decide the shape.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g1s sort defining.
invariants: A shape's defining attributes must stay fixed while colour, size and orientation vary.
misconceptions: Treating colour, size or orientation as if it decided what a shape is.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same shape?

explanationVariants: Sort by what defines the shape.
Then the groups are truly alike.

widget.prompt: What makes a shape a rectangle?

options.label: 4 straight sides and 4 square corners
options.feedback: Correct — a rectangle has 4 straight sides and 4 square corners; colour, size, and direction can change.

options.label: Being red
options.feedback: Color can change freely without the shape changing; it is not a defining attribute.

options.label: Being large
options.feedback: Size can change freely without the shape changing; a tiny rectangle is still a rectangle.

options.label: Pointing upward
options.feedback: Turning a shape does not change what it is; orientation is not a defining attribute.

steps.body: Objects can also be sorted by colour. The picture groups red buttons and blue buttons, but colour does not decide the name of a shape.
steps.narration: Objects can also be sorted by colour. The picture groups red buttons and blue buttons, but colour does not decide the name of a shape.

widget.prompt: Tap the shape that belongs in the 4-sided group.

hotspots.label: triangle
hotspots.feedback: A triangle has 3 straight sides, so it belongs with the 3-sided group.

hotspots.label: circle
hotspots.feedback: A circle has no straight sides at all, so it joins neither group.

hotspots.label: small triangle
hotspots.feedback: Size is non-defining; with 3 sides it still belongs in the 3-sided group.

widget.missFeedback: Count the straight sides, then choose the group that matches.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — 4 straight sides puts the rectangle in the 4-sided group.

widget.prompt: How many corners does a triangle have?

commonErrors.feedback: That counts one more corners than a triangle actually has; trace around it once and stop where you began.
That misses one corners; the last one closes the triangle back to the start.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Look again at the shape's sides and corners, counting each one exactly once.

widget.prompt: Which of these can change WITHOUT a triangle stopping being a triangle?

options.label: Its color
options.feedback: Correct — color can change to anything and the shape is still a triangle.

options.label: Its number of sides
options.feedback: Change the number of sides and it stops being a triangle — that attribute defines it.

options.label: Its number of corners
options.feedback: Corners are a defining attribute; changing them changes what the shape is.

options.label: Whether its sides are straight
options.feedback: Straight sides are part of what a triangle is; curving them makes a different shape.
